properties.title: Pimenta Bueno 1987
properties.description:
On June 3, 1987, six squatters were killed in confrontation: Valdir Viana, Antonio de Jesus, José Alves da Silva, Francisco F. da Silva, José Luiz de Oliveira F. and Dalvino Viana. The friction occurred because of the possible limit of the possessions of each group, given the delay in the process of expropriation and settlement of the 400 families living in this area of 10,000 hectares in the municipality of Pimenta Bueno (RO).
INCRA claimed that there was no conflict in the region and that there were no resources to implement the project. The land was under conflict at least since 1980, when a conflicted firefight had left eight dead.

properties.title: Vilhena / Espigão 1987
properties.description:
Six people were killed in conflict in the Roosevelt indigenous area for trying to take possession of the land, in dispute between the Cinta Larga Indians and farmers denounced since 1975 for plotting the land for deforestation practices and for the entry of squatters. The dead squatters were José Carneiro, Claudinei Elias de Morais, Josias Ribeiro Gomes, Valdemir Pereira, David de Jesus Gomes and Diomar Ferreira Maia. Over the years several indigenous peoples were killed in traps. After this massacre, the Federal Court established injunction that annulled the permissions for the exploitation of the indigenous reserve by logiers who, even then, even built points on the river Aripuana for passage of wood.
(Photo: CEDOC Dom Tomás Balduino)

Os posseiros mortos foram José Carneiro, Claudinei Elias de Morais, Josias Ribeiro Gomes, Valdemir Pereira, Davi de Jesus Gomes e Diomar Ferreira Maia. No decorrer dos anos diversos indígenas foram mortos em armadilhas. Após este massacre, a Justiça Federal estabeleceu liminar que anulava as permissões para exploração da reserva indígena por madeireiras que, mesmo assim, chegaram a construir pontos sobre o rio Aripuana para passagem de madeira.

properties.title: Colméia 1986
properties.description:
Since the 1950s, many farmers lived and worked at Vale do Juari Farm in Colméia (TO). The area was known as Union land. In 1971, the Goiani businessman José Fleury Curado came out claiming to be owner of the region, generating many conflicts and deaths in sequence. In 1979, the land was sold by him to the farmer Luiz Espindola Cardoso. Several eviction injunctions were granted to the farmer. In one of these, on March 7, 1986, the farmer, accompanied by his sons, gunmen and military police officers, officially evicted 36 families, burning the houses. In action, a man, a woman and a child were killed. It was only in November 1988 that the farmers signed public deed transferring the Vale do Juari Farm to the Union for the purposes of Agrarian Reform.
(Photo: CEDOC Dom Tomás Balduino)
properties.description (Portuguese, as published):
Desde a década de 1950, muitos lavradores moravam e trabalhavam na Fazenda Vale do Juari, em Colméia (TO). A área era conhecida como sendo terra da União. Em 1971, o empresário goianiense José Fleury Curado surgiu afirmando-se proprietário da região, gerando muitos conflitos e mortes em sequência. Em 1979, a terra é vendida por ele ao fazendeiro Luiz Espindola Cardoso. Várias liminares de despejo foram concedidas ao fazendeiro. Em uma destas, no dia 07/03/1986, o fazendeiro, acompanhado de seus filhos, de pistoleiros e de policiais militares, despejou oficialmente 36 famílias, queimando as casas. Na ação, um homem, uma mulher e uma criança foram mortos. Apenas em novembro de 1988 é que os fazendeiros assinaram escritura pública transferindo a Fazenda Vale do Juari para a União com fins de Reforma Agrária.
(Foto: CEDOC Dom Tomás Balduino)

properties.title: Salto do Jacuí 1989
properties.description: Known as the “Massacre of Santa Elmira”, published in a book by Franciscan Friar Sérgio Görgen, this case combines the eviction of 500 families violently by the police, the illegal imprisonment of more than 20 without lands that were tortured with beating, threats with revolvers, forced to lie naked on anthills and gas poisoning, in addition to the murder of six children when a plane that threw pesticides in the soybean crops of the region passed over the camp of Rincão do Ivaí with the open squirts. There were approximately 1300 to 3800 conflicting hectares. Several other conflicts and violence followed in this which was one of the most serious land incidents in Rio Grande do Sul.
properties.description (Portuguese, as published): Conhecido como “Massacre da Santa Elmira”, publicado em livro de autoria do frei franciscano Sérgio Görgen, este caso combina o despejo de 500 famílias de forma violenta pela polícia, a prisão ilegal de mais de 20 sem terras que foram torturados com espancamento, ameaças com revólveres, obrigados a deitarem-se nus sobre formigueiros e intoxicação por gás, além do assassinato de seis crianças quando um avião que jogava agrotóxicos nas lavouras de soja da região passou sobre o acampamento de Rincão do Ivaí com os esguichos abertos. Havia aproximadamente 1300 a 3800 hectares conflitivos. Diversos outros conflitos e violências se seguiram neste que foi um dos mais graves incidentes de terra no Rio Grande do Sul.

properties.title: Sarandi / Passo Fundo 1986
properties.description: The month of March 1986 was marked by demonstrations of approximately 300,000 small farmers gauchos against high interest rates and the government's misdefinition of agricultural policy. On March 31, 1986, during the blockade of BR-386, a truck would have lost the brake, seriously injuring several farmers and killing three: Lirio Grosseli, Vitalino More and Roseli Salete Nunes da Silva. A CPI of violence concluded that the driver Valdir José da Silva was guilty of the accident, intentional. The story of this conflict was portrayed ten years later by filmmaker Tetê Moraes in the documentary “The Dream of Rose”.

Uma CPI da violência concluiu que o motorista Valdir José da Silva foi culpado pelo acidente, intencional. A história deste conflito foi retratada dez anos depois pela cineasta Tetê Moraes no documentário “O sonho de Rose”.

properties.title: Uberlândia 2012
properties.description:
Three members of the Landless Liberation Movement (MLST) were found shot to the head on the state highway MG-455, near the district of Miraporanga in Uberlândia (MG): Nilton Santos Nunes, Valdir Dias Ferreira and Celestina Leonor Sales Nunes. A child, granddaughter of Nilton and Celestina and niece of Valdir, only five years old, was in the car where they were killed and was found by firemen in shock. Six people were targeted in the police inquiry. Four were convicted in June 2015 99 years ago in prison and the other two were cleared. If I didn't send her for land dispute, the crime would have occurred out of revenge on Celestina, who would have denounced the drug trafficking by the group that promoted the killing.
(TV Integration)
properties.description (Portuguese, as published):
Três integrantes do Movimento de Libertação dos Sem Terra (MLST) foram encontrados mortos com tiro na cabeça na rodovia estadual MG-455, próximo ao distrito de Miraporanga em Uberlândia (MG): Nilton Santos Nunes, Valdir Dias Ferreira e Celestina Leonor Sales Nunes. Uma criança, neta de Nilton e Celestina e sobrinha de Valdir, de apenas 5 anos, estava no carro em que foram mortos e foi encontrada pelos bombeiros em estado de choque. Seis pessoas foram apontadas no inquérito policial. Quatro foram condenadas em junho de 2015 há 99 anos de prisão e as outras duas inocentadas. Se não a mando por disputa de terra, o crime teria ocorrido por vingança a Celestina, que teria denunciado o tráfico de drogas pelo grupo que promoveu a chacina.

properties.title: Felisburgo 2004
properties.description:
On November 20, 2004, 200 families who occupied the Nova Alegria Farm (since 2002 constituting the Camp Promised Land), of 2400 hectares, in Felisburg (MG), were surprised by shots fired by 18 gunmen coordinated by Adriano Cafisco Luedy, who says he owns the land, considered to be returned, but not yet settled by the slowness of the judiciary. In the attack, twenty workers were shot and wounded and five others were killed: Iraguiar Ferreira da Silva, Miguel José dos Santos, Francisco Nascimento Rocha, Juvenal Jorge da Silva and Joaquim José dos Santos. The perpetrator, Adriano Cafisco, who was on the run, was arrested 13 years later, on December 14, 2017, in Salvador (BA), and will serve 115 years in prison.
(Photo: MST)

properties.title: Unaí 2004
properties.description:
Three tax auditors and the driver of the Ministry of Labor were murdered in the municipality of Unaí (MG), on 28/01/2004, when they made an inspection against slave labor on farms in the region, respectively: Nelson José da Silva, João Batista Soares Lages, Erastotles de Almeida Gonçalves and Ailton Pereira de Oliveira. They were approached by men who shot at the car in which they were on the clover known as Seven Plates, on the MG-188 road.
Twelve years after the murder, the nine suspects were convicted. Of nine defendants, three hired executioners were arrested (Rogério Alan Rocha Rios, Erinaldo de Vasconcelos Silva and William Gomes de Miranda), one of the principals died before being convicted (Francisco Helder Pinheiro), but four other convicts still answer in freedom. The leaders are political and economic names in the region: Antherio Mânica (former mayor elected twice in Unaí), Norberto Mânica, Hugo Alves Pimenta and José Alberto de Castro. Your sentences reach 100 years each.
(Photo: SINAIT)

properties.title: Colniza 2017
properties.description:
Nine squatters of the Settlement Project (P.A.) Taquaruçu do Norte were killed by four gunmen, hired by a timber businessman, on April 19, 2017. The group came into the community, broke into the shacks and killed the nine squatters with 12-gauge gunfire and machete blows. Some of the victims were killed while working the land. According to forensics, there was torture, as several bodies were bound and two of the victims were cut to death. The site of the slaughter is within the ‘Guariba Complex’, an area of 630,000 hectares that houses a plot of 42,000 hectares, where the workers worked.
The region is subject to intense agrarian conflict due to its high timber and mining potential. Colniza, a municipality that covers the gleba of Taquaruçu do Norte, is located 1,065 kilometers from the capital of Mato Grosso and borders the states of Amazonas and Rondônia. The city is identified as one of the most violent cities in Brazil by the large number of agrarian conflicts.
(Photo: Caio Motta)

properties.title: Terra Nova do Norte 1990
properties.description:
Farmer Clemente de Almeida Souza Neto, known as “Quele”, landowner conflicting with 52 families in Gleba União and 200 in Pingo D’Água since the entry of the squatters into the land in 1985, carried out several attacks, with threats, assassination attempts and murders. On October 15, 1990, he attacked a family, torturing and killing four people: Creuza Cardoso de Oliveira, Franciene, José P. Martins de Souza and Raimundo Ferreira de Souza. In the case of Franciene, in an act of perversity, the criminals cut off and broke in half his head, which was transported a mile away.
With the arrest decreed, the farmer was only found by Sinop's civilian police while traveling to the state of Tocantins. Exactly one year after the crime, the case was submitted to a popular jury, which sentenced Quele to 67 years in prison and the jagunço Sinval do Nascimento France to 35, constituting the first case of murder against squatters in which the perpetrator of the crime was tried and convicted in the state of Mato Grosso. Less than two years later, through the corruption of a military police officer, both fled the prison and remained on the run. The CPT followed and denounced each new fact of the case.

O fazendeiro Clemente de Almeida Souza Neto, conhecido como “Quele”, proprietário de terra conflitando com 52 famílias na Gleba União e 200 na Pingo D’Água desde a entrada dos posseiros na terra em 1985, efetuou diversos ataques, com ameaças, tentativas de assassinato e assassinatos. No dia 15/10/1990 atacou uma família, torturando e matando quatro pessoas: Creuza Cardoso de Oliveira, Franciene, José P. Martins de Souza e Raimundo Ferreira de Souza. No caso de Franciene, em um ato de perversidade, os criminosos deceparam e partiram ao meio sua cabeça, que foi transportada há um quilômetro de distância.
Com a prisão decretada, o fazendeiro só foi encontrado pelo policiais civis de Sinop enquanto viajava para o estado do Tocantins. Exatamente um ano após o crime, o caso foi submetido a júri popular, que condenou Quele a 67 anos de prisão e o jagunço Sinval do Nascimento França a 35, constituindo o primeiro caso de assassinato contra posseiros em que o mandante do crime foi julgado e condenado no estado de Mato Grosso. Menos de dois anos depois, por meio da corrupção de um policial militar, ambos fugiram da penitenciária e se mantiveram foragidos. A CPT acompanhou e denunciou cada novo fato do caso.

properties.title: Santa Leopoldina 2002
properties.description:
On 15/08/2002, six people from three generations of the same family were murdered in the district of Cocal, in Santa Leopoldina (ES). The family was half owned by Adolfo Seick. They died: Lena Souza Calote, Orlando Cruz de Mendonça, Maria de Lourdes Cruz, Nicolau Pagung, Luciana Pagung and Fabiana Pagung. The bodies were found scattered, indicating escape. The victims had some severed limbs.
Landowners, hoping to sell them without indemnifying the family who lived on the land for so many years, were arrested as suspects: Adolfo Seick, Ermindo Seick, Erick Boldt and Dirceu Berger, in addition to the employee of another farm, Luiz Augusto Felisberto, who claimed to have witnessed the massacre. His reports found support in the forensics of the Legal Medical Institute (IML) and the investigation was conducted, condemning the suspects and detaining the mayor of the city at the time, Idemar Edringuer, alleged buyer of the lands, who, responding in freedom, was acquitted on a popular jury in 2012.

A família era meeira da propriedade que pertencia a Adolfo Seick. Morreram: Lena Souza Calote, Orlando Cruz de Mendonça, Maria de Lourdes Cruz, Nicolau Pagung, Luciana Pagung e Fabiana Pagung. Os corpos foram encontrados espalhados, indicando fuga. As vítimas tiveram alguns membros decepados.
Proprietários das terras, na expectativa de vendê-las sem indenizar a família que residia na terra há tantos anos, foram detidos como suspeitos: Adolfo Seick, Ermindo Seick, Erick Boldt e Dirceu Berger, além do funcionário de uma outra fazenda, Luiz Augusto Felisberto, que afirmou ter testemunhado o massacre. Seus relatos encontraram respaldo na perícia do Instituto Médico Legal (IML) e a investigação foi conduzida, condenando os suspeitos e detendo o prefeito da cidade à época, Idemar Edringuer, pretenso comprador das terras, que, respondendo em liberdade, foi absolvido em júri popular em 2012.

properties.title: Canavieiras 1985
properties.description: Surrounded by about twenty gunmen on a boat in the municipality of Canavieiras, four squatters were killed: José Cardoso Filho, Raimundo Osmar Alves, João Batista Cardoso dos Santos and João Mineiro. In the conflict, as a reaction, the squatters killed two gunmen. In the area, sub judice since 1979, other attacks and murders were recorded. In the conflict, on the one hand, Eulina do Nascimento is declared landowner. In 1982, Gerson Alves do Vale buys the right to land. In 1984, Dely Dias dos Santos (known as “Dely Ruim”, the boss of the massacre, according to the confession of gunmen in 1986) claims to have bought the right to land. On the other hand, dozens of squatters who, even with titles registered in court, have suffered numerous extrajudicial actions over the years. From the request of FETAG and CPT, an Interministerial Commission (Ministry of Justice, MIRAD, INCRA and Federal Police) was established to survey the ownership of the land in the registries of the region. In November of the same year, INCRA received the land for resettlement program.

No conflito, como reação, os posseiros mataram dois pistoleiros. Na área, sub judice desde 1979, foram registradas outras investidas e assassinatos. No conflito, de um lado, Eulina do Nascimento se declara proprietária da terra. Em 1982, Gerson Alves do Vale compra o direito a terra. Em 1984, Dely Dias dos Santos (conhecido como “Dely Ruim”, mandante do massacre, conforme confissão de pistoleiros em 1986) afirma ter comprado o direito a terra. Do outro lado, dezenas de famílias posseiras que, mesmo com títulos registrados em cartório, sofreram inúmeras ações extrajudiciais ao longo dos anos. A partir de solicitação da FETAG e da CPT, foi constituída uma Comissão Interministerial (Ministério da Justiça, MIRAD, INCRA e Polícia Federal) para levantamento sobre a posse das terras nos cartórios da região. Em novembro do mesmo ano, o INCRA recebeu as terras para programa de reassentamento.

properties.description:
Known internationally, the Magave case refers to the massacre of five members of this family, brutally killed and quartered at Campo Alegre farm: Nadir Vieira de Castro Magave, Iracy de Castro Magave, Osmar de Castro Magave, Áurea Cambraia de Castro Magave and Alcides de Castro Magave, who had occupied the land since the 1950s, having been regularized by INCRA since 1975 on their 571 hectares of land, were murdered between the days 03 and 04/02/1994. The boundaries of the property were questioned by neighbors Aderbal Távora and the Santa Clara company. The investigation condemned four gunmen involved in the crime, who then benefited from penalty reductions. Aderbal Távora, accused of being the boss, was arrested preventively, but died of cancer in 1996.
